## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components with a mask intermediate can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout at 69 B/particle offers 41% hot bytes in loop 1 (28 of 68 B: age+pos+vel), only 5% in loop 2 (4 of 68 B: seed), and 41% in loop 3. The mask intermediate adds 1 B/particle — verdict kept in a byte stream, not registers. The approach fuses integrate+decide into loop 1 writing the mask, then loop 2 scans it for respawn via select-based (`csel`) logic and byte-granular scatter. With 68 B/particle and 128 B cachelines, roughly 1.9 particles share a line, so the 59% dead weight in loop 1 and 95% in loop 2 is dragged through the filler on every access. Working set spills L1d at N≈949 and L2 at N≈60787.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p is strikingly flat across regimes: 7.6 in L1d (N=380), a mild rise to 8.1 at N=10000 (L2-resident), then settling back to 7.4–7.5 in DRAM (N≥62000). Neither the L1d→L2 transition at N≈949 nor the L2→DRAM spill at N≈60787 produces a visible knee. If anything, DRAM-resident points are marginally faster than L2 points, suggesting L2 associativity pressure exceeds streaming-DRAM cost. The dense grid resolves no sharp cache event — cost is dominated by per-particle compute and the branchy respawn, not residency.

## Bandwidth
The memory floor is 2.308 ns/p; at q=0.01 the algo runs 7.4–8.1 ns/p, achieving 8.5–9.3 GB/s — only ~30% of the 29.9 ceiling. This is compute-bound at low q: profiles show 58–66% compute, 28% backend stall, 3–6% branch_flush. As q rises, bandwidth collapses to 7.0–7.5 GB/s at q=0.25 and 5.6–5.9 GB/s at q=0.5, with branch_flush climbing to 20%. Against baseline: 1.01–1.05x at q=0.01 (marginal win), 0.92–1.04x at q=0.1 (tied), 0.86–0.90x at q=0.25 (loses), 0.88–0.93x at q=0.5 (loses). Against the winner: 1.6–2.3x slower everywhere — the branchy respawn is the equalizer that erases any vectorization gain.

## Assembly
Loop 1 achieves partial vectorization: `fmul.4s`, `fadd.4s`, `fmul.2s`, `fadd.2s`, `ext.16b`, `dup.4s` process pos/vel, but 7 scalar FP ops remain and an indexed gather (`ld1.s {v2}[1]`) breaks the streaming pattern. Loop 2 is the bottleneck: 416 insns/iter, 91 cond-branches, 18 `csel`, 16 byte-granular `strb`, and 35 `bl` calls to spawn — fully unrolled into 32 individual `ldrb`/`cbz`/`bl` sequences with no vectorization. Only 9 of 539 instructions are vector-suffixed across the entire step. The byte-scatter `strb` stores and per-spawn function calls cap achieved bandwidth at ~30% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — 1.01–1.05x baseline at q=0.01 (marginal) but 0.86–0.93x at q≥0.25 (loses to naive), and 1.6–2.3x slower than the winner at every N×q point. The partial loop-1 vectorization (6 vec FP ops on 41%-hot bytes) cannot compensate for the 416-instruction, 91-branch, byte-scatter respawn loop that dominates as death rate rises, and the 5%-hot loop 2 wastes 95% of streamed bandwidth through the line filler.
